title: The Savoy as a teenager; Central Avenue instead of 52nd Street
summary: He got into New York ballrooms as a tall teenager, and says his 52nd Street was really Central Avenue in Los Angeles.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: When you were in New York, you said you signed with William Morris, and they sent your trio out to all these different areas of the country. But did you spend much time in New York? You mentioned going to the Savoy at some point. How about 52nd Street? You were there when 52nd Street was happening, weren't you?
No, I wasn't in New York when 52nd Street... I was living out in California then. But you mentioned... What did you just ask me?
Well, when you were in New York, you said you went to the Savoy.

Oh, that was when I was a teenager. I mean, I was real young then. See, I was tall for my age. I must have been, you know, 13 or 14 or 15. I used to get in these places, and since I didn't drink, nobody ever bothered me.

But 52nd Street to me was Central Avenue. Because when 52nd Street was really hopping, I was living out here and working out on Central Avenue and in Hollywood, and Billy Berg's and places like that. So I saw 52nd Street, but I never did really work on 52nd Street.
